story.title: The Obituary Pilot
story.logline: A grieving radio host realizes the live callers to his midnight show are reading their own death notices.
story.theme: Fate cannot be rescheduled, no matter how fast you talk.
story.twist: The final caller is the host himself, broadcasting from the wreckage of his own studio.
story.ending: A haunting reminder that every countdown eventually hits zero.

scenes.narration: My midnight radio show never gets callers, until the phone rings with a voice reading my own obituary.
scenes.visual_prompt: Close up of Leo, 30, tired eyes, messy dark hair, wearing a black hoodie, sitting inside a dark radio booth with glowing red mics.
scenes.camera: Extreme close up on his face, pushing in rapidly.

scenes.narration: Leo stares at the studio console as the mysterious caller hangs up, leaving only a cold dial tone behind.
scenes.visual_prompt: Medium shot of Leo, 30, messy dark hair, black hoodie, staring at the lit-up phone line inside the dark radio booth.

scenes.narration: Another line lights up instantly, and a woman describes the exact floral arrangement resting at her own funeral.
scenes.visual_prompt: Medium shot of Leo, 30, messy dark hair, black hoodie, hands shaking over the audio board in the dark radio booth.

scenes.narration: Panic grips my chest because I recognize every single detail they speak as an unprinted front-page newspaper story.
scenes.visual_prompt: Close up of Leo, 30, messy dark hair, black hoodie, sweating under the studio lights inside the dark radio booth.

scenes.narration: Leo tries to cut the broadcast feed, but the master switch snaps off in his bloody, trembling fingers.
scenes.visual_prompt: Close up of Leo, 30, messy dark hair, black hoodie, struggling with the studio control board inside the dark radio booth.

scenes.narration: The studio speakers echo a familiar voice reading tomorrow morning headlines before anyone else even knows they happened.
scenes.visual_prompt: Medium shot of Leo, 30, messy dark hair, black hoodie, backing away from the microphone inside the dark radio booth.

scenes.narration: A loud siren wails outside the window as flashing red lights paint the walls of the quiet broadcasting room.
scenes.visual_prompt: Wide shot of Leo, 30, messy dark hair, black hoodie, trapped inside the dark radio booth as red light flashes.

scenes.narration: Leo rushes to the glass window, watching emergency crews swarm the exact building he is currently broadcasting from.
scenes.visual_prompt: Medium shot of Leo, 30, messy dark hair, black hoodie, pressing his hands against the studio glass in the dark room.

scenes.narration: The studio phone rings one final time, and the voice on the other end whispers that my shift is over.
scenes.visual_prompt: Close up of Leo, 30, messy dark hair, black hoodie, lifting the telephone receiver inside the dark radio booth.
scenes.camera: Extreme close up on the phone.

scenes.narration: Leo listens to the dead air, finally realizing the broadcast started long after he stopped breathing.
scenes.visual_prompt: Wide shot of an empty, wrecked radio booth with flashing red lights, no sign of Leo, 30, messy dark hair, black hoodie.

caption.hook: His midnight callers were already dead.
caption.title: The Obituary Pilot
caption.caption:
Arthur thought he was just playing late-night requests. Then the voice on line three read word-for-word from tomorrow's paper. Some broadcasts are impossible to cancel.

Would you answer if your final hour was on the air?
